title: MLB Pitcher Arsenal 2020-2026
subtitle: Every pitcher's pitch mix, velocity, spin, break, whiff% and run value
description:
# MLB Pitcher Arsenal 2020-2026

What every MLB pitcher threw in the **2020-2026 regular seasons**, pitch type by pitch type: how often, how hard, how much spin and break, and how it worked (whiff rate, put-away rate, run value, xwOBA). All numbers come from Baseball Savant's own leaderboards, fetched and checked by a public build script.

## What changed in this version (September 2026)

The previous version (one file, `pitcher_arsenal_evolution_2020_2025.csv`) was computed by hand from raw pitches and had errors:

- **`whiff_rate` was wrong.** It divided swinging strikes by swings *plus called strikes*, so it was far too low (2025 four-seam median 0.132, against Savant's 21.6%). `whiff_pct` here is Savant's whiff%: swinging strikes / swings.
- **It was not regular season only.** Pitches from March 1 to November 30 were used, so spring training and the postseason were mixed in. This version is regular season only (checked pitch by pitch for three pitchers against Statcast search restricted to regular-season games).
- Pitchouts (PO) and unclassified pitches were treated as pitch types, one row had no name, and names were lowercase.
- 2026 was missing.

This version replaces that file (and the notebooks and README that shipped with it) with three new CSVs. They keep the same pitchers: 99.8% of the old file's pitcher-seasons are in the new wide table (the rest pitched only in spring or the postseason, e.g. Shane McClanahan 2020).

## Files

| File | Rows | One row per | Rows per season (2020 / 2021 / 2022 / 2023 / 2024 / 2025 / 2026) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pitcher_arsenal.csv` | {rows:pitcher_arsenal} | pitcher, season, pitch type | {rows:pitcher_arsenal:2020} / {rows:pitcher_arsenal:2021} / {rows:pitcher_arsenal:2022} / {rows:pitcher_arsenal:2023} / {rows:pitcher_arsenal:2024} / {rows:pitcher_arsenal:2025} / {rows:pitcher_arsenal:2026} |
| `pitcher_arsenal_wide.csv` | {rows:pitcher_arsenal_wide} | pitcher, season (12 pitch types side by side) | {rows:pitcher_arsenal_wide:2020} / {rows:pitcher_arsenal_wide:2021} / {rows:pitcher_arsenal_wide:2022} / {rows:pitcher_arsenal_wide:2023} / {rows:pitcher_arsenal_wide:2024} / {rows:pitcher_arsenal_wide:2025} / {rows:pitcher_arsenal_wide:2026} |
| `arsenal_changes.csv` | {rows:arsenal_changes} | pitcher, season, pitch type, compared with the season before | – / {rows:arsenal_changes:2021} / {rows:arsenal_changes:2022} / {rows:arsenal_changes:2023} / {rows:arsenal_changes:2024} / {rows:arsenal_changes:2025} / {rows:arsenal_changes:2026} |

**`pitcher_arsenal.csv`** (the main table): pitches, usage %, run value (total and per 100 pitches), whiff %, K %, put-away %, BA/xBA, SLG/xSLG, wOBA/xwOBA, hard-hit %, launch angle, exit velocity, barrel %, average speed, spin, horizontal and vertical break (with and without gravity), release point, and break compared with similar pitches (speed and release) with its percentile.

**`pitcher_arsenal_wide.csv`**: the same numbers, one row per pitcher-season, with throwing hand, arm angle and ten metrics for each pitch type (`ff_usage_pct`, `sl_whiff_pct`, `ch_avg_spin`, ...).

**`arsenal_changes.csv`**: for every pitcher who pitched in consecutive seasons, each pitch type's previous value, current value and change in usage, speed, spin, break, whiff % and run value per 100, with `is_new` / `is_dropped` flags for pitches added or dropped.

Pitch types: FF four-seam, SI sinker, FC cutter, SL slider, ST sweeper, SV slurve, CU curveball, CH changeup, FS splitter, FO forkball, SC screwball, KN knuckleball.

## Things to know

- **Every pitcher is included** (Savant's lowest thresholds): pitch types with at least one plate appearance ending on them come from Savant's Pitch Arsenal Stats. Pitch types that were thrown but never ended a plate appearance are added from Savant's Pitch Arsenals page with usage, speed, spin and break only (`in_arsenal_stats` = False). Filter on `pitches` or `total_pitches` for stable rates.
- **Knuckle curves are counted as curveballs** (Savant's arsenal pages do the same). Eephus pitches, pitchouts and unclassified pitches are not listed, so a pitcher's `usage_pct` can add up to a little less than 100.
- **Sweepers (ST)** are labelled back to 2020 by Savant, so a pitch reclassified between seasons appears in `arsenal_changes.csv` as one new and one dropped type.
- `break_x_vs_similar` / `break_z_vs_similar` (Savant's Pitch Movement comparison) exist only for the pitchers that leaderboard lists: about half of all rows, and 98.4-99.6% of pitch types thrown 250+ times. `arm_angle` exists for the pitchers Savant's Arm Angle leaderboard lists (roughly a third of pitchers).
- 2026 is the complete 2026 regular season (it ended on September 27, 2026).
- Pat Venditte (switch-pitcher, 2020) has one Savant row per hand on the Pitch Arsenals page; his 2020 speed, spin and break are left empty.

## How it is built and checked

[build.py](https://github.com/yasumorishima/kaggle-datasets/blob/main/pitcher-arsenal-dataset/build.py) fetches each season from Baseball Savant (Pitch Arsenal Stats, Pitch Arsenals, and Pitch Movement and Pitcher Arm Angle through [savant-extras](https://pypi.org/project/savant-extras/) 0.6.0). Savant answers a request it does not understand with the *current* season, so the season of every answer is verified, and the build publishes nothing unless every check passes:

- every table has exactly the seasons 2020-2026, with a minimum number of rows and pitchers per season;
- no two seasons of any source table are the same table, or nearly the same (most shared pitchers with identical numbers);
- the core pitch types FF, SI, FC, SL, ST, CU and CH are present in every season;
- usage adds up to 97-100.6% for at least 99.5% of pitchers with 100+ pitches;
- the median whiff % of each main pitch type is in a plausible range every season (measured medians: four-seamers 21.1-22.0%, sliders 32.4-36.8%);
- at least 98% of stats rows got speed, spin and break, and the old version's pitcher-seasons are still covered.

## Data source

[Baseball Savant](https://baseballsavant.mlb.com/) (MLB Advanced Media), regular seasons 2020-2026.
